note: Measurements follow the ranges and means of Tables 33/34; the original gives the alate table as n=3♀, 7♂ (same colony) and the soldier as n=7. Bacchus (1987: 72) described the species from only 2 soldiers.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate is difficult to distinguish from C. darlingtone, differing only in the slightly smaller measurement range; the soldier differs in its very small, distinctly recessed genal horns — the frontal horns completely conceal the genal horns in anterodorsal view, whereas in C. darlingtone the genal horns remain visible in that view. A very rare humid-forest species, possibly already extinct in Barbados. Distribution: Barbados and St Vincent in the Lesser Antilles; not recorded elsewhere. The neotype designated in the original was collected at Vermont Falls Trail, St Vincent, where the alate caste was also first described. Bacchus (1987) described the species from only 2 soldiers and 1 colony.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Uniformly pale brown; sclerotized veins brown, wing membrane nearly transparent, very faintly smoky brown; head, labrum and pronotum pale brown; the pale brown chevron mark on the forewing scales almost invisible; antennae pale brown; abdominal tergites yellowish brown, sternites very pale yellowish brown; femora whitish, tibiae and other distal parts pale yellowish brown. Head oval, cranial suture distinct; compound eyes medium-sized, slightly straight-edged along the antennal sockets; ocelli medium-sized, oval, almost touching the compound eyes. Antennae 15—17 segments, mostly 16, formula variable, usually 2=3=4=5. Pronotum wider than long, anterior and posterior margins slightly concave, sides moderately convex; a cruciform mark and a dorsal median line visible. Radius of forewing merging with the costa beyond half the wing length; radial sector with more than 5 branches. Arolium present. Table 33 measurements (n=3♀, 7♂, same colony): head length including labrum 1.10—1.16 mm (mean 1.14), head length to postclypeus 0.82—0.87 (0.83), head width (maximum at the compound eyes) 0.88—0.93 (0.91), compound eye long diameter 0.29—0.33 (0.31), minimum distance from the compound eye to the posterior margin of the head 0.13—0.18 (0.16), ocellus diameter 0.10—0.13 (0.12), pronotum length 0.59—0.65 (0.61), width 0.83—0.92 (0.88), body length with wings 8.80—9.51 (9.18), body length without wings 3.98—5.54 (4.57), forewing length 6.82—7.53 (7.20), maximum width 1.88—2.13 (2.00), hind tibia length 0.75—0.82 (0.78).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule in dorsal view almost black in the anterior 2/3, becoming rusty to rusty orange posteriorly; in lateral view the anterodorsal region black, the posteroventral region behind the compound eyes rusty orange. Mandibles dark chestnut-brown. Anterior margin of the pronotum rusty, the rest pale yellow, with a brown patch only on the anterior half. Head in dorsal view nearly square, posterior margin rounded, sides very slightly constricted behind the frontal shield; weak wrinkled depressions at the anterolateral corners and behind the frontal shield; a round median depression on the vertex; wrinkles deep and long. Frontal shield slightly raised, wrinkled, very shallowly concave in dorsal view, with a median notch, and this notch is not continuous with the vertex depression; the frons forms 90° with the vertex. Frons wrinkled, with paired depressions on either side of a distinct median longitudinal ridge. Labrum short, slightly swollen at the middle. Frontal horns prominent in dorsal view, thumb-like, wrinkled. Genal horns very small, conical, directed anterodorsally, invisible in dorsal view; in lateral view the frontal and genal horn bases meet, the frontal horn about 5 times the volume of the genal horn; the genal horns distinctly recessed behind the dominant frontal horns. Mandibles with a wrinkled swelling on the basal 1/3, dentition short. Eye spots oval, distinctly pigmented. Antennae 12—14 segments, mostly 13 or 14, formula variable, usually 2>3>4<5 or 2>3<4=5. Pronotum broadly shield-shaped, anterior margin bluntly truncate, posterolateral corners rounded. Table 34 measurements (n=7, same colony): head length including frontal shield 1.28—1.38 mm (1.33), head length including mandible tips 1.59—1.65 (1.63), head length including frontal horns 1.32—1.42 (1.38), frontal shield width 1.13—1.21 (1.17), outer distance between frontal horns 0.87—0.92 (0.90), head width 1.16—1.23 (1.19), head height (excluding postmentum) 0.95—1.05 (0.98), pronotum width 1.03—1.21 (1.14), length 0.74—0.83 (0.79), left mandible length 0.63—0.72 (0.67), total length 3.56—4.90 (4.20).

sections.label: Other
sections.text: The holotype soldier from Barbados could not be found in the AMNH collection, and the only paratype was lost while being prepared for SEM; the original therefore designated a neotype soldier and a new paratype series, the neotype colony being from Vermont Falls Trail, St Vincent, 13°13.00′N, 61°12.90′W, 1998-v-25, collected by JK, BM and JM, comprising 1 neotype soldier, 6 new paratype soldiers and 1 SEM specimen, alate morphotypes and 9 paratype alates, and immatures (STV109).
